criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-10-03 has mechanism naming the new function path in crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs and the status.rs line function (no longer "none"), owner still Apollo, and a measure ending in `status: not shown` or a label printed by `athena status`; Grep of the entry shows it.
criteria.evidence: I grepped docs/spec.toml lines 1546-1552. The mechanism names `crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs later_similar_task` and `crates/athena-core/src/status.rs later_similar_task_line`. The owner is still "Apollo". The measure is "cargo test -p athena-data later_similar_task; the later similar task: line of athena status; status: not shown". Both functions exist in the diff.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs shows: with an accepted proposal and a later same-class landed job with no recurrence, the check reports prevented; with a later recurrence at an earlier stage it reports detected earlier; with a recurrence at the same or later stage, or with no records, it reports not shown. Run `cargo test -p athena-data introspection`; the test fails if the function body is stubbed to always report not shown.
criteria.evidence: All 5 tests in later_similar_task_tests pass: prevention, earlier detection, same/later stage not shown, no records / no later job not shown, and before-acceptance / unaccepted. The tests use assert_eq!(..., LaterTask::Prevented) and LaterTask::DetectedEarlier, so a stub that always returns NotShown would fail them. I read this from the code; I did not run a stub because I must not change files. One gap: the code has no notion of a 'same-class landed job', so the prevented test passes with job(11) or job(12) of any class (see the soundness finding).

criteria.criterion: `athena status` output includes the new later-similar-task line, with the status.rs unit test and a crates/athena-cli test asserting the line equals the StatusView field for both shown and not-shown outcomes. Run `cargo test -p athena-core status` and `cargo test -p athena-cli status`.
criteria.evidence: These tests pass: status::improvement_cycle_line_tests::the_later_task_line_names_each_outcome_and_empty_records_are_not_shown (athena-core) and status_prints_the_later_similar_task_line_for_both_outcomes (athena-cli tests/status_build_measurement.rs). The cli test checks that the printed line equals view.later_similar_task for the not-shown case (empty fixture) and for the shown (prevented) case. display.rs prints v.later_similar_task.

criteria.criterion: A recurrence of the same class before the proposal was accepted, or a proposal that is only pending or rejected, does not count as the improved process (checked by a negative test in the same test module).
criteria.evidence: The test a_recurrence_before_acceptance_or_an_unaccepted_proposal_does_not_count passes. It checks that a recurrence only before job 10 is not shown, and that Pending, Rejected and Withdrawn proposals with a later landed job are not shown. The code skips any proposal whose status is not Accepted and splits introspections at j > accepted.

findings.summary: 'Prevented' counts any later landed job as a 'similar task', although the records do carry each job's class of work.
findings.evidence: The doc comment says "Records carry no class for a landed job, so any later landed job stands for a later task." That is false. The Job record has `class_of_work: Option<String>` (crates/athena-data/src/records.rs line 607), and JobRecords holds `job: Option<Job>` (crates/athena-core/src/store.rs line 28). In the evidence snapshot, 1896 files under records/jobs carry a non-null class_of_work. ProposalRecord also has `applies_to` (classes of work), and the accepted reading named `class_of_work in applies_to` as the matching key. As written, once any proposal is accepted, the next unrelated job that lands (say a docs typo fix) makes `athena status` print `later similar task: shown (prevented)`. That is a false success on the one line meant to show OLY-10-03, against the outcome-check and no-empty-success defaults. A more correct approach: pass each landed job's id together with its class_of_work, and count only later landed jobs whose class is in the proposal's applies_to (or that match the failure class). If a job has no class, it should not count.
findings.location: crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs later_similar_task (the `landed.iter().any(|j| j > accepted)` branch and its doc comment)

findings.summary: 'Prevented' is decided from a single later landed job, and returns early on the first accepted proposal.
findings.evidence: `return LaterTask::Prevented` fires as soon as one landed job sorts after the accepting job. It does not wait for a minimum number of later similar jobs, and it stops checking other accepted proposals that may show recurrences. One job without a recurrence is weak evidence of prevention. A minimum count of later same-class jobs would be sounder.

findings.summary: The detection-stage ranking assumes a 'failed' introspection is an earlier catch than 'rejected'.
findings.evidence: `failed` covers a job that failed on its own run, which can be an infrastructure or host failure rather than the defect being caught. Ranking it ahead of 'rejected' as 'detected earlier' is a guess. Every other category, including owner interventions such as 'mistake' and 'fixed-environment' seen in the snapshot, is lumped together at rank 2.

summary: The change adds `later_similar_task` to athena-data and a `later similar task:` line to `athena status`, and fills in the mechanism and measure for OLY-10-03 in docs/spec.toml (owner still Apollo). All five criteria are met. The targeted tests I ran pass (`cargo test -p athena-data introspection`, `cargo test -p athena-core status`, `cargo test -p athena-cli status`), and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. The verdict is still fail because of a major soundness problem. The requirement is about a later *similar* task, but the code counts any job that lands after the proposal was accepted as one. Its doc comment justifies this by saying the records carry no class for a landed job, which is false: job records have `class_of_work` (set in 1896 files in the evidence snapshot), and proposals have `applies_to`. As a result, once any proposal is accepted, the next unrelated job that lands makes status print `shown (prevented)`, a false success. Only later landed jobs whose class matches the proposal should count. Two smaller issues: one later job is enough to report 'prevented', and the ranking that treats 'failed' as an earlier catch than 'rejected' is a guess.
